security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, validation messages, or expected zip packaging behavior. I found no prompt-injection text, credential handling, network calls, or covert command execution. One semantic issue remains: init_skill.py does not validate the supplied skill name before creating directories and files.

remediation.issue: init_skill.py accepts skill names from argv without enforcing the documented hyphen-case rules before filesystem writes.
remediation.suggestion: Reject names that do not match the documented pattern, reject path separators, and verify the resolved skill directory stays under the requested output directory before mkdir or write_text.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Controls File Creation Path
semantic_findings.description: init_skill.py reads skill_name from argv and appends it to the output path before creating directories and files. The script prints naming rules but does not enforce them before filesystem writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code uses unvalidated command-line input to build a directory path and then creates that path. The issue depends on an agent or user passing an unsafe skill name, so confidence is high but impact is bounded to local file writes.

content.user_title: Create AI Skills With Reusable Workflows
content.value_statement: Building reliable AI skills requires clear structure, reusable resources, and validation steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through skill design, initialization, editing, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md frontmatter and body structure.
Guides planning for scripts, references, and assets.
Provides init_skill.py for generating a starter skill folder.
Provides quick_validate.py for frontmatter and naming checks.
Provides package_skill.py for creating .skill zip packages.
Includes reference patterns for workflows and output templates.
limitations: Generated templates still require human domain content.
Validation checks structure and metadata, not task quality.
Packaging includes files inside the chosen skill folder.
No network publishing or marketplace upload is included.

use_cases.title: Create a New Assistant Skill
use_cases.description: Plan the skill purpose, choose resource folders, generate a starter structure, and prepare it for validation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Skill Documentation
use_cases.description: Use the guidance to write concise frontmatter, body instructions, workflow steps, and output patterns.

use_cases.title: Package Skills for Sharing
use_cases.description: Validate a completed skill folder and create a distributable package for handoff or review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me plan a new skill for [task]. Ask only the essential questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Starter Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a new folder from the template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to initialize a skill named [skill-name] in [target folder]. Include scripts and references only if they are useful.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the skill at [path]. Tighten the trigger description, remove unnecessary files, and improve validation readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Skill for Distribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to validate, fix, and package the skill at [path]. Explain any remaining risks before packaging.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for PDF form workflows.
output_examples.output: A practical skill plan with the trigger description, recommended scripts, reference documents, validation steps, and packaging actions.
A concise revision plan that removes vague guidance, adds reusable resources, and clarifies when the skill should trigger.
A validation result, a short list of fixes if needed, and a prepared distributable skill package.

best_practices: Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed references into separate files.
Use scripts only when they make repeated work more reliable.
Validate the skill folder before packaging or sharing it.
anti_patterns: Do not add broad documentation files that are not needed by the agent.
Do not hide trigger guidance inside the body instead of frontmatter.
Do not package placeholder files that should have been removed.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI skills with clear instructions, reusable resources, validation steps, and packaging support.

faq.question: Does it write the domain content for me?
faq.answer: It provides structure and guidance, but the author must supply accurate domain knowledge and examples.

faq.question: Can it update an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide revisions to frontmatter, instructions, resource organization, validation, and packaging.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful for skills intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it publish skills to a marketplace?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and packages skills, but it does not upload or publish them.

faq.question: What should I check before packaging?
faq.answer: Check that frontmatter is complete, resource files are needed, placeholders are removed, and validation passes.
